hot.title: Do Language Models Need Sleep? Offline Recurrence for Improved Online Inference
hot.summary: An "LLM sleep" mechanism enables Transformer-based models with fast-weight memories to perform offline recurrent passes for memory consolidation, enhancing their ability to perform deep reasoning on information evicted from the active attention window. This approach consistently improves task performance on benchmarks like cellular automata and math reasoning by allowing iterative processing of past contexts without increasing real-time inference latency.

hot.title: When Does LeJEPA Learn a World Model?
hot.summary: Research by Klindt, LeCun, and Balestriero formally defines and proves the conditions under which a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA), specifically LeJEPA, learns a "World Model" by recovering the true underlying latent variables. It demonstrates that LeJEPA achieves linear identifiability if and only if the latent variables follow an isotropic Gaussian distribution, which then enables optimal latent-space planning.

hot.title: Qwen-VLA: Unifying Vision-Language-Action Modeling across Tasks, Environments, and Robot Embodiments
hot.summary: Qwen-VLA, developed by the Qwen Team, unifies diverse embodied decision-making problems such as robot manipulation and vision-language navigation into a single vision-language-action model. This unified framework achieved an 83.6% average success rate on real-world ALOHA manipulation tasks and demonstrated strong generalization, including outperforming previous specialist models on specific dynamic manipulation benchmarks.

hot.title: Gemini Embedding 2: A Native Multimodal Embedding Model from Gemini
hot.summary: Google's Gemini Embedding 2 is a native multimodal embedding model capable of creating unified vector representations for video, audio, image, and text, including interleaved combinations. The model achieved state-of-the-art performance across multimodal retrieval benchmarks with a global mean score of 77.2, and demonstrated superior native audio understanding, outperforming ASR-based baselines by +3.59 mrr@10 on the MSEB benchmark.

hot.title: The MiniMax-M2 Series: Mini Activations Unleashing Max Real-World Intelligence
hot.summary: MiniMax developed the M2 series, a family of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models designed for agentic tasks, demonstrating that models with approximately 10 billion activated parameters can achieve competitive performance against leading frontier models. The M2 series integrates agent-driven data pipelines, a scalable reinforcement learning system called Forge, and early self-evolution capabilities to enhance real-world intelligence.

hot.title: MUSE-Autoskill: Self-Evolving Agents via Skill Creation, Memory, Management, and Evaluation
hot.summary: MUSE-Autoskill presents a comprehensive agent framework that enables large language model agents to autonomously create, manage, evaluate, and refine their own reusable skills, integrating a five-stage skill lifecycle and multi-level memory system. This approach leads to a 7.16 percentage point improvement in task accuracy with self-generated skills and allows for the transfer of these skills across different agent architectures, improving another agent's performance by 10.51 percentage points.

hot.title: From Pixels to Words -- Towards Native One-Vision Models at Scale
hot.summary: NEO-ov, developed by S-Lab, NTU, and SenseTime Research, introduces a native, encoder-free vision-language model that unifies single-image, multi-image, and video understanding with spatial intelligence through an end-to-end autoregressive architecture. The model establishes new performance benchmarks for native VLMs, matching or surpassing leading modular counterparts on various reasoning and perception tasks, and showing strong spatial intelligence comparable to specialist models.

hot.title: LocateAnything: Fast and High-Quality Vision-Language Grounding with Parallel Box Decoding
hot.summary: LocateAnything is a vision-language framework that introduces Parallel Box Decoding (PBD) to enable the simultaneous generation of entire bounding box units, overcoming the sequential decoding bottleneck in visual grounding. This method achieves a greater than 10x speedup in decoding throughput and improves localization accuracy, for example, by 3.8% in mean F1-score on LVIS over previous methods, setting new benchmarks across diverse visual perception tasks.

hot.title: CUA-Gym: Scaling Verifiable Training Environments and Tasks for Computer-Use Agents
hot.summary: CUA-GYM introduces an agentic pipeline for generating large-scale, verifiable Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) training data for computer-use agents, comprising 32,112 tasks across 110 real and synthesized environments. This approach improved agent performance on the OSWorld and WebArena benchmarks and led to the emergence of efficient multi-action tool calling.

hot.title: Gamma-World: Generative Multi-Agent World Modeling Beyond Two Players
hot.summary: Gamma-World is a generative multi-agent world model designed for interactive simulation, introducing Simplex Rotary Agent Encoding for permutation-symmetric agent identities and Sparse Hub Attention for efficient cross-agent communication. The model demonstrates superior video fidelity (e.g., FVD 184.1 vs 333.8 for Solaris) and scalability (linear computational cost with agents) compared to baselines, enabling real-time interactive rollouts and zero-shot generalization to more agents.

hot.title: SkillOpt: Executive Strategy for Self-Evolving Agent Skills
hot.summary: SkillOpt introduces a text-space optimization framework for refining natural-language agent skills, allowing frozen large language models to acquire and adapt procedural knowledge. The method achieves consistent performance gains across various benchmarks and models, improving average accuracy by up to +39.0 points on specific procedural tasks while generating compact and transferable skill artifacts.

hot.title: Scaling World-Model Reinforcement Learning Through Diffusion Policy Optimization
hot.summary: Model-Based Diffusion Policy Optimization (MBDPO) unifies policy search and optimization within world models using a diffusion process, regularized by an implicit energy function learned from data. This approach consistently achieves superior performance and sample efficiency across diverse control tasks, while demonstrating robust scalability in multi-task pretraining and mitigating value overestimation.

hot.title: Recursive Flow Matching
hot.summary: Recursive Flow Matching (RecFM) introduces a generative framework for forecasting complex spatiotemporal dynamics, achieving high physical accuracy and computational efficiency by enforcing self-consistency across discretization scales. This approach demonstrates competitive or superior performance across scientific benchmarks with significantly fewer inference steps, such as a 20x speedup over diffusion-based emulators.

hot.title: AutoScientists: Self-Organizing Agent Teams for Long-Running Scientific Experimentation
hot.summary: AUTOSCIENTISTS is a decentralized, self-organizing multi-agent framework designed to conduct long-running scientific experimentation without central coordination. The system achieved a 74.40% mean leaderboard percentile on BioML-Bench, 1.9x acceleration in GPT training optimization, and improved protein fitness prediction by 6.5% on ProteinGym.

hot.title: LLaVA-OneVision-2: Towards Next-Generation Perceptual Intelligence
hot.summary: Researchers at Glint Lab, AIM for Health Lab, and MVP Lab developed LLaVA-OneVision-2, a vision-language model that processes video as a continuous bit-cost stream, shifting from traditional frame-centric paradigms to leverage native video codec structures. This approach improves temporal grounding, fine-grained event localization, and spatial reasoning, outperforming baselines by 4.3 points on video understanding tasks and achieving a 74.9 mAP on a new jump-rope benchmark.

hot.title: Qwen-Image-Bench: From Generation to Creation in Text-to-Image Evaluation
hot.summary: Qwen-Image-Bench, a benchmark from Alibaba co-developed with professional artists, introduces "Real-world Fidelity" and "Creative Generation" dimensions to evaluate Text-to-Image models beyond basic metrics. Its human-supervised Q-Judger offers fine-grained diagnostics, effectively differentiating state-of-the-art models and highlighting systemic limitations in handling implicit world knowledge and reasoning.

hot.title: Looped Diffusion Language Models
hot.summary: Researchers from KAIST, KRAFTON, and UC Berkeley introduced LoopMDM, an architecture integrating selective looping into masked diffusion models. This approach allows LoopMDM to achieve competitive or superior performance while significantly reducing training FLOPs by up to 3.3x and demonstrating enhanced capabilities in math reasoning tasks compared to deeper non-looped baselines.

hot.title: Long Live The Balance: Information Bottleneck Driven Tree-based Policy Optimization
hot.summary: Information Bottleneck-driven Tree-based Policy Optimization (IB-TPO) addresses the exploration-exploitation imbalance in online reinforcement learning for large language models. The framework, which includes a novel IB-Score metric and an IB-guided tree sampling strategy, improved accuracy by 2.9% to 3.6% over GRPO baselines on mathematical reasoning and multi-task benchmarks, while also enhancing sampling efficiency.

hot.title: Self-Improving Language Models with Bidirectional Evolutionary Search
hot.summary: Researchers at Harvard and MIT developed Bidirectional Evolutionary Search (BES), a framework that integrates evolutionary operators with a backward search for goal decomposition, enabling language models and agentic systems to discover higher-quality solutions. The method showed performance gains of up to 3.8% on multi-hop reasoning for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and consistently outperformed baselines on open problem-solving tasks like Circle Packing and Heilbronn problems.

hot.title: HumanEgo: Zero-Shot Robot Learning from Minutes of Human Egocentric Videos
hot.summary: HumanEgo introduces a framework enabling robots to learn bimanual manipulation skills directly from minutes of human egocentric video, achieving zero-shot transfer to diverse robot platforms without any robot-specific data. The system demonstrates an average 92.5% success rate across four complex manipulation tasks, outperforming existing baselines and matched-time robot teleoperation.

likes.title: Perception Encoder: The best visual embeddings are not at the output of  the network
likes.summary: Perception Encoder introduces a family of vision models that achieve state-of-the-art performance across diverse vision and vision-language tasks, demonstrating that general, high-quality visual features can be extracted from the intermediate layers of a single, contrastively-trained network. It provides specific alignment tuning methods to make these features accessible for tasks ranging from zero-shot classification to dense spatial prediction and multimodal language understanding.

likes.title: TTRL: Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: TTRL is a framework enabling Large Language Models to self-improve through Reinforcement Learning on unlabeled test data, using self-generated rewards derived from majority voting. This approach substantially boosts performance on complex reasoning tasks, with one model achieving a 211% improvement on AIME 2024, by fostering a self-reinforcing learning loop.

likes.title: Inference-Time Scaling for Generalist Reward Modeling
likes.summary: DeepSeek-AI and Tsinghua University developed Self-Principled Critique Tuning (SPCT) and DeepSeek-GRM models, a pointwise generative reward modeling approach that achieves state-of-the-art performance in generalist reward benchmarks. This method demonstrates effective inference-time scalability, allowing smaller models to match or exceed the performance of much larger models by leveraging increased compute during inference, thereby improving LLM alignment.

likes.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
likes.summary: Research from Tsinghua University reveals that current Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) primarily enhances the sampling efficiency of Large Language Models for already existing reasoning patterns. This optimization often narrows the models' overall reasoning capacity at higher pass@k values, contrasting with distillation, which effectively expands their problem-solving scope.

likes.title: Reasoning Models Can Be Effective Without Thinking
likes.summary: Ma et al. demonstrated that Large Language Models trained for Chain-of-Thought reasoning can achieve comparable or superior performance without generating explicit reasoning steps, utilizing a technique called 'NoThinking'. This approach significantly reduces inference latency by up to 9x and token usage by up to 5.1x, particularly when combined with parallel sampling, offering a more efficient paradigm for LLM reasoning.

likes.title: Synthetic Data Generation & Multi-Step RL for Reasoning & Tool Use
likes.summary: SWiRL is an offline multi-step reinforcement learning methodology designed to enhance Large Language Models' reasoning and tool-use capabilities. It generates and utilizes synthetic data, applying process-based filtering for step-wise optimization, which leads to substantial performance gains and strong cross-domain generalization in complex tasks.

likes.title: ReTool: Reinforcement Learning for Strategic Tool Use in LLMs
likes.summary: ReTool, developed by ByteDance Seed, introduces a reinforcement learning framework that enables Large Language Models to strategically use code interpreters for complex problem-solving. It achieved 67.0% accuracy on the AIME 2024 benchmark, significantly improving performance over text-based reasoning and demonstrating emergent self-correction capabilities in code generation.

likes.title: Hogwild! Inference: Parallel LLM Generation via Concurrent Attention
likes.summary: Researchers from Yandex, HSE University, and IST Austria developed "Hogwild! Inference," a protocol enabling multiple Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate text concurrently by sharing a dynamically updated attention Key-Value (KV) cache. This mechanism allows LLMs to self-organize and collaborate in real-time, achieving up to 3.6x speedup and improved accuracy on complex reasoning tasks.

likes.title: Challenges and Paths Towards AI for Software Engineering
likes.summary: This paper presents a strategic roadmap for the field of AI in software engineering, providing a comprehensive taxonomy of software development tasks and identifying nine key bottlenecks that impede current AI capabilities. It proposes a targeted set of research directions focused on data collection, training, and inference-time approaches to advance automated software development.

likes.title: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
likes.summary: Researchers from ByteDance Seed, Tsinghua University, and The University of Hong Kong developed DAPO, an open-source reinforcement learning system for large language models. The system achieved 50 points on the AIME 2024 dataset with a Qwen2.5-32B model, surpassing the prior 47-point score of DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B while requiring 50% fewer training steps.

likes.title: Proof or Bluff? Evaluating LLMs on 2025 USA Math Olympiad
likes.summary: Researchers from ETH Zurich and INSAIT conducted the first evaluation of large language models on generating rigorous natural language proofs for problems from the 2025 USA Mathematical Olympiad. The study found that most state-of-the-art models scored below 5% of the maximum points, with the highest-performing model, GEMINI-2.5-PRO, achieving only 24.4%, demonstrating fundamental shortcomings in advanced mathematical reasoning capabilities.

likes.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: DeepSeek-AI developed DeepSeek-R1, an LLM demonstrating that sophisticated reasoning capabilities can emerge through pure outcome-based reinforcement learning without reliance on human-annotated reasoning trajectories. The model achieved an AIME 2024 pass@1 accuracy of 77.9% with R1-Zero, and the multi-stage DeepSeek-R1 surpassed state-of-the-art models on numerous math, coding, and STEM benchmarks while exhibiting emergent self-reflection and dynamic strategy adaptation.

likes.title: ReSearch: Learning to Reason with Search for LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: The ReSearch framework enables Large Language Models to integrate multi-step reasoning with external search, learning interactively via reinforcement learning without supervised intermediate steps. It yields substantial performance gains on complex multi-hop question answering benchmarks and reveals emergent self-correction capabilities.

likes.title: Insights into DeepSeek-V3: Scaling Challenges and Reflections on Hardware for AI Architectures
likes.summary: DeepSeek-V3 showcases how a hardware-software co-design strategy can achieve state-of-the-art large language model performance using a comparatively modest cluster of 2,048 NVIDIA H800 GPUs. The paper highlights innovations like Multi-head Latent Attention, DeepSeekMoE, FP8 mixed-precision training, and a Multi-Plane Fat-Tree network, which collectively reduce memory consumption, lower training costs, and accelerate inference.

likes.title: One-Minute Video Generation with Test-Time Training
likes.summary: Researchers from NVIDIA and leading universities introduce Test-Time Training (TTT) layers within pre-trained Diffusion Transformers to generate one-minute-long videos from text storyboards, enabling coherent multi-scene narratives while addressing the computational limitations of traditional self-attention mechanisms for long sequences.

likes.title: Sequential Task Assignment and Resource Allocation in V2X-Enabled Mobile Edge Computing
How new data permeates LLM knowledge and how to dilute it
likes.summary: Research from Google DeepMind reveals how new knowledge permeates through large language models, demonstrating that surprising information (measured by token probability) leads to broader changes across model behavior, while introducing "stepping-stone" text augmentation and "ignore-k" update pruning techniques that reduce undesirable priming effects by 50-95%.

likes.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
likes.summary: Titans introduces a new neural memory module that learns to memorize information at test time and effectively combines with attention mechanisms for better long-term sequence modeling

likes.title: PHYBench: Holistic Evaluation of Physical Perception and Reasoning in  Large Language Models
likes.summary: PHYBench, a new benchmark developed by the School of Physics at Peking University, rigorously evaluates large language models' physical perception and reasoning using 500 original, human-curated physics problems. Evaluations revealed a substantial performance gap between LLMs and human experts, with the best LLM achieving 36.9% accuracy compared to the human baseline of 61.9%.

likes.title: Process Reward Models That Think
likes.summary: This research introduces THINKPRM, a generative process reward model that enables large language models to provide verbalized, long Chain-of-Thought (CoT) verification for their reasoning steps. The model, developed by a collaboration including University of Michigan and LG AI Research, achieves high performance with orders of magnitude less step-level supervision than traditional discriminative models, while significantly improving reliability and generalizability.
